summary.text: Micah Jones, a Republican attorney who has represented clients before the SEC, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the open Massachusetts 6th District seat to Dan Koh.
An Army veteran who served with the 82nd Airborne Division, including in Afghanistan, he is a former Democrat who became an independent and then a Republican.

paragraphs.text: Jones served in the U.S. Army from 2011 to 2016, predominantly with the 82nd Airborne Division, including a deployment to Afghanistan from 2014 to 2015.
He earned a bachelor's degree from the University of California, San Diego, and a law degree from Northeastern University School of Law, which he says he paid for using the GI Bill.
Jones works as an attorney representing clients before the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, including in SEC investigations and litigation.
He says this role barred him from trading individual stocks and that members of Congress should be held to the same standard.
Jones describes himself as a former Democrat and told Fox News he left the party around 2016, during law school, and became an independent before joining the Republican Party.
In the 2026 race he said the district's seat was open for the first time in 47 years and that he would seek to work with the administration where appropriate.
He was unopposed in the September 1 Republican primary.
During the campaign, he described himself as center-right on fiscal issues and said his campaign was built on three priorities: accountability, opportunity and security.
He received 36.6% of the vote to Dan Koh's 63.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
He describes himself as a husband and father.
